newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Aug 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Aug 6.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Wednesday:
* Ford said sales of its cars and light trucks rose 5.0 percent in July.
* The index of leading economic indicators registered no increase in June, despite the continued surge in stock prices.
* Nynex president and group executive for external affairs, Donald Reed, is expected to announce his resignation.
* Viacom reported a loss for the second quarter.
* The Cable News Network named former ABC news executive Richard Kaplan as president of its U.S. news unit.
* The Nasdaq rose on Tuesday, while the Dow Industrials fell, as did bond prices.
* Thailand agreed to increase taxes and reorganize its financial industry in return for an IMF-led rescue package.
* The strike at United Parcel Service slowed the company's business nearly to a halt.
* Officials in several American cities said they are exploring plans to sell water from their own municipal water supplies.
* President Clinton signed bills that put into place a balanced budget.
* Russia's Oneksim Bank won a 38.0 percent stake in Norilsk Nickel in a privatization auction.
* Either Estee Lauder founders' Estee or Ronald Lauder or their estates will face a huge tax bill under the new tax law signed by President Clinton.
* The founder of Oxford Health Plans, Steven Wiggins, resigned.
* Insurance companies have a new way to protect themselves from natural disasters: issue bonds to investors.
